CODE OF PRACTICE FOR SEAWORTHY PACKING OF UNMANUFACTURED CIGARETTE TYPE TOBACCO
0.

FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 29 July 1968, after the draft finalized by the Tobacco Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 In view of customs restrictions on the moisture content of imported tobacco and its high tariff rates, it is imperative for the overseas buyers to This code has been insist on a perfect waterproof packing of the material. prepared so as to co-ordinate the requirements of overseas buyers and the It covers the packing of untrade practices prevailing in the country. manufactured tobacco of cigarette type only. 0.3 Two types of packing, namely, wooden cases and jute gunny or hessian bales are generally employed for unmanufactured cigarette type tobacco. The type of packing is so chosen as to suit the country of destination and the form of tobacco, which may be in strips or leaves or bits. Tobacco is exported to the West European countries mainly in the form of strips which Bulk of tobacco meant for Asian and East are packed in wooden cases. European countries is packed in jute gunny or hessian bales. 0.3.1 There are two types of jute gunny or hessian bale packings in vogue, namely, bales with ropes ! ordinary bales ) and bales without ropes ( Rhodesian type). Ordinary bales are more popularly adopted by exRhodesian type packing prevents porters to almost all the destinations. cake formation as the tobacco parked in this manner is not sub.jected to pressure by ropes and there is scope for tobacco to expand to full volume This type of packing is employed for certain specific of the container. consignments to countries like the United Kingdom. 0.4 \Vhile formulating this standard due consideration has been given the prevailing trade practices in the country and also to the views overseas buyers. to of

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers the seaworthy packing procedure of unmanufactured cigarette type tobacco. It also prescribes the materials for packing in wooden cases and in jute gunny or hessian bales. 2. PACKING IN WOODEN CASES

2.1 Packing Materials -The wooden cases employed in the packing A shall be of either 122 x 76 x 76 cm size or 100 x 83 x 63 cm size. polyethylene liner ( see Grade 2 13 of IS : 2508-I 963* ) of 40-micron thickness and having an extra length of 2.25 cm than that of the case shall be used. For both the sizes of the cases, bitumen laminated waterproof paper (see Type 1 of IS : 1398-19607 ) may also be used. 2.2 Packing Procedure-Spread the tobacco in layers, one upon the other in the case lined with the polyethylene film or bitumen laminated waterproof paper ( 2.1) . Press the strips firmly from one end to the other The redried tobacco may end of the case by using a thick wooden plank. be delivered mechanically into the cases by a conveyor belt, and uniformly spread over and pressed. Press the tobacco in a hydraulic press to a density of 304 kg/m3 and to a level 7 to 10 cm below the edge of the case. Seal the polyethylene bag preferably by means of electric heater by pressing the two edges. 2.3 Weight of the PackageThe gross weight of the case shall he 175 to 250 kg and the net weight shall be 135 to 205 kg.
NOTE For this case weight, board thickness as given in Class A of Table 1 and any one of the species of timber as given in Appendix .A of IS : 1503-1967~ may be used for the manufacture of packing cases.

3.1.3 Packing Procedure-Place a piece of jute cloth ( 3.1.1) of 90 x 60 cm dimension mto a bale charger, and place 60 to 70 g kraft paper of the Keep it ready at the delivery end of the machine. same dimension over it. Lay the tobacco straight at the feeding end on apron of the redrying In case of strips lay them in the tangled manner straightening machine. as far as possible. While arranging the tobacco uniformly in the charger, press the former with a wooden plank till the charger is filled to give a net weight of about 100 kg. Place a piece of kraft paper of 150 x 90 cm dimension, followed by a piece ofjute cloth of the same dimensions on the top of the charger. Subsequently, press the tobacco in a hydraulic press the thickness of tobacco to about to a density of 336 kg/m3, reducing 42 to 45 cm. While the bale is still in the press, fasten a rope (3.1.1) about 9 times over the entire length of the bale keeping a distance of about Tie the rope tight 8 cm in between the two and 15 cm from either edge. Stitch the edges at the joints of the and release the pressure on the bale. front gunny piece. Cover the top and bottom of the bale with kraft paper and jute cloth and stitch with a two-fold jute twine (3.1.1). Finally, pass a sealing wire through both the edges of gunny pieces and through the eyelets of the lead seal which are fixed on either side and the eyelet of Seal both the the Agmark label which is fixed on one side of the bale. lead seals by punching them with Agmark pliers. 3.1.4 Weight of the Bale-The gross and the net weight of the bale shall be 103 kg and 100 kg respectively. 3.2 Packing in Bales Without Ropes ( Rhodesian Type)
